description: CTE (WITH clause) coverage across the DML/DDL combinations the core CTE suites do not exercise: CREATE TABLE AS SELECT from a CTE and from a recursive CTE, CREATE VIEW over a CTE, UPDATE ... FROM and DELETE ... USING a CTE-shaped derived table, an empty CTE, and a CTE inside an UPDATE SET subquery. Converted 1:1 from dml/CteDmlCoverageTest (now retired).

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE src (id INTEGER, v INTEGER)
INSERT INTO src VALUES (1,10),(2,20)
CREATE TABLE dst AS WITH c AS (SELECT id, v * 2 AS v2 FROM src) SELECT id, v2 FROM c
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM dst
SELECT v2 FROM dst WHERE id = 1
CREATE TABLE nums AS WITH RECURSIVE r(n) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM r WHERE n < 5) SELECT n FROM r
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM nums
SELECT MAX(n) FROM nums
CREATE TABLE src (id INTEGER, v INTEGER)
INSERT INTO src VALUES (1,10),(2,20)
CREATE VIEW vw AS WITH c AS (SELECT id, v FROM src WHERE v > 15) SELECT * FROM c
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM vw
SELECT id FROM vw
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, v INTEGER)
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1,0),(2,0)
CREATE TABLE s (id INTEGER, nv INTEGER)
INSERT INTO s VALUES (1,100),(2,200)
UPDATE t SET v = c.nv FROM (WITH c AS (SELECT id, nv FROM s) SELECT * FROM c) c WHERE t.id = c.id
SELECT v FROM t WHERE id = 1
SELECT v FROM t WHERE id = 2
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER)
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1),(2),(3)
CREATE TABLE removals (id INTEGER)
INSERT INTO removals VALUES (2)
DELETE FROM t USING (WITH c AS (SELECT id FROM removals) SELECT * FROM c) c WHERE t.id = c.id
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM t
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM t WHERE id = 2
CREATE TABLE e (id INTEGER)
WITH c AS (SELECT * FROM e) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM c
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, v INTEGER)
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 0)
UPDATE t SET v = (WITH c AS (SELECT 99 AS x) SELECT x FROM c) WHERE id = 1
SELECT v FROM t WHERE id = 1
